name: Atorvastatin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Atorvastatin needs no dose adjustment in kidney impairment because kidney disease does not change its blood levels (US label). Kidney impairment is a risk factor for myopathy, so muscle symptoms should be watched.

hd.text: Not studied in end-stage renal disease; hemodialysis is not expected to enhance clearance (highly protein bound) (label). No label adjustment.

pd.text: No data in label; no label adjustment.
pd.short: No PD data; no label adjustment

dialyzable: Not expected to be significantly removed by hemodialysis (label).
monitoring: Muscle symptoms (myopathy, rhabdomyolysis); renal impairment is a risk factor (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and homozygous FH (HoFH): 10 years and older. Not established under 10 years or for other hyperlipidemias (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: HeFH: 10 mg once daily, range 10 to 20 mg. HoFH: 10 to 20 mg once daily, range 10 to 80 mg (label gives fixed doses, not mg/kg).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney data; adult label has no kidney adjustment. Specialist input.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label has no kidney adjustment. Specialist input.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label has no kidney adjustment. Specialist input.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label has no kidney adjustment. Specialist input.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
